correctness.rationale: For every N>=3, shifted block equality is equivalent to a length-2m run of digit-sum differences D_m=1. Factoring m=2^e u reduces any such run to at least 2u-1 complete q blocks. If odd u>=3, five adjacent q contain two consecutive aligned pairs; each pair imposes 2-adic valuation -1 modulo N on consecutive integers, impossible. For m=2^e, the carry identity 1-v2(q+1) gives the exhaustive start intervals and earliest start. These are all-parameter implications; direct independent checks of 3,932,160 instances are additional corroboration, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The May 2025 motivating source states a result for twist powers j not congruent to 1 modulo N and explicitly poses the excluded j=1 boundary. The present theorem proves a complete dyadic root-length and valuation-position characterization in precisely that excluded case. Full 2007 prior work analyzes ordinary powers, not these cyclically letter-shifted block triples. Searches of indexed claims and web literature found no equivalent classification, but historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: A 2025 study singles out the excluded one-step cyclic twist as a natural unresolved boundary. The complete all-moduli classification identifies exactly which infinite root-length family survives, gives every starting interval, and proves a sharp earliest-occurrence formula. The dyadic rigidity and 2-adic windows are structural rather than finite coincidences, with potential use in twisted pattern avoidance and automatic-word factor recognition.
